cards.explanation: The answer is that the place is too small for them. The sons of the prophets tell Elisha, "Please take note that the place where we meet with you is too small for us." (2 Kings 6:1) I know that feeling, friends, because my first bakery counter had room for me, one mixing bowl and a whole lot of elbow bumping.

The answer is True. The sons of the prophets ask to go to the Jordan and get a log each, and Elisha answers with one word: "Go." (2 Kings 6:2) No speech, no list of rules. Just a green light, and a short one.

The answer is that he asks Elisha to come along with them. A man says, "Please come with your servants." (2 Kings 6:3) He wants Elisha to walk out there with them. I'd like to think a crew works better when the leader shows up too, but that's just me talking.
The answer is True. Elisha answers, "I will come…" (2 Kings 6:3) Short and sweet, and he doesn't make anybody beg. Verse 4 says Elisha went with them.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, "As one of them was cutting down a tree, the iron axe head fell into the water." (2 Kings 6:5) The head comes off mid-chop and lands in the water. I've dropped a lot of things in my day, but never something into a whole river.

The answer is "borrowed." He cries out, "Oh, my master, it was borrowed!" (2 Kings 6:5) I bet that one word is the whole worry. Losing your own tool is bad enough, but I think losing someone else's makes your stomach drop.
The answer is "Where did it fall?" The man of God asks exactly that. (2 Kings 6:6) That's a question about the spot, nothing else. No scolding, no lecture, and I'll admit I'd have had a lot to say.

The answer is a stick. The man of God "…cut a stick, threw it there, and made the iron float." (2 Kings 6:6) Plain wood, nothing fancy. I've got a whole bakery of tools, friends, and I'd never have guessed this one.

The answer is that the iron floats. The man of God threw the stick there "…and made the iron float." (2 Kings 6:6) An iron axe head sinking is what you'd expect, friends, and that's the point. I'll say it again, IRON FLOATED.
The answer is False. Elisha says, "Lift it out…" and the man "…reached out his hand and took it." (2 Kings 6:7) No diving, no swimming, no wet apron. He reaches out and the iron is right there.
